source.title: Cavite Flood Mitigation for Lowland Areas - Environmental Impact Statement
source.provider: Department of Public Works and Highways; Japan International Cooperation Agency; KRC Environmental Services Inc.
source.fishEvidenceLocation: Section 4.3.3, printed pp. 4-139 to 4-163; Table 4.40 and Table 4.47.

aquaticEcologySurvey.dateContext: The report says the aquatic ecology assessment was conducted on these dates; Table 4.40 gives station-specific date/time.
aquaticEcologySurvey.surveyDesign: Four stations focused along proposed channel boundaries in a brackish-water river/estuary/mangrove/abandoned-fishpond project area. The report calls this a dry-month snapshot and says it cannot evaluate seasonal variation.
aquaticEcologySurvey.fishDataBasis: Table 4.47 labels its data source as Direct observations and interviews. The narrative says fish were caught at different surveyed stations and most sampled fish were tilapia. No standardized fish gear, per-taxon capture method, identification protocol, voucher or catalog number is provided.

tableLegend.A: Abundant: source says caught in enormous quantities by fishers.
tableLegend.C: Common: source says frequently seen or represented in the catch.
tableLegend.R: Rare: source says seldom seen/caught and few in number.

taxa.taxonomyResolution: source spelling is a GBIF Backbone synonym; accepted name is Terapon jarbua
source provides alternative genus-level names; no species resolution

taxonomyCrosscheck.method: Strict exact-name GBIF Backbone API matches for five species-rank strings. Source spellings are preserved; these matches verify nomenclatural usage only, not field identification or specimen identity.

projectSummaryCrosswalk.decision: Matching project context and counts make the EIA a plausible detailed source for the aggregate. Without an explicit cross-reference, keep the JICA Volume 1 aggregate unassigned and use only the EIA matrix for documented station-locality evidence.

rights.decision: Keep minimal attributed facts in the internal research ledger only. Do not reproduce the table, source prose, figures or maps; do not publish species rows until reuse rights and independent field-identification review are resolved.

limitations: Table 4.47 combines direct observations and interviews and does not identify the evidence mode per taxon-by-station cell.
The sampling dates are historical and the report calls the assessment a dry-month snapshot; no current presence or seasonal completeness is established.
No fish gear, per-row catch date, fish identification procedure, voucher or specimen catalog number is provided.
Three fish rows remain genus-level or alternative-genus records; exact GBIF Backbone matches do not validate field identifications.
Only Station 4 is explicitly at the Maalimango River mouth; Stations 1-3 remain source-described localities and are not assigned to named waterbodies here.
The brackishwater description applies to the mouth station only; no whole-river salinity class is established.
The EIA is publicly accessible but item-specific reuse terms are unverified; no public projection is approved.
No permitted channel geometry, fishing access, current catchability, fishing legality or safety conclusion is established.
nextAction: Seek authorized, dated source data for Bacoor, Cavite San Juan and Labac; request or locate the CvSU 2014 Labac fish study. The licensed Boothroyd national stream-network check did not provide a local Maalimango trace (nearest modeled line was about 16 km away in the Marikina_Pasig catchment). An OSM same-name Maalimango reach is associated with Pasong Kawayan I/II in General Trias and is not assigned to the Rosario source locality; see calabarzon-maalimango-hydrography-crosscheck-20261029.json. Keep Maalimango geometry unresolved and seek a permitted, higher-resolution channel source. Keep this matrix research-only pending taxonomy, field-identification and reuse review; do not infer missing species.
